clue.text: Soundness of article about clerical employment

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
C is short for circa, about
a curacy is the post held by a curate, a junior clergyman

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece questions whether an article on jobs in the Church is reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of a statement or reckoning means its correctness and precision.

clue.text: A page with little desire for food

parts.note: petite means small

explanation.surface: A young servant who is not very hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger is the wish to eat.

clue.text: A Spaniard caught Italians out.

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish fielder takes catches to dismiss the Italian batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns ITALIANS into ASTILIAN after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Castile, the central Spanish region, is a Spaniard.

clue.text: Went mounted — love to make a show

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Riding horseback for love of putting on a display.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy show of riding and roping skills, with bucking broncos.

clue.text: Accommodating many people in a small house causes criticism

indicators.note: accommodating means housing within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a cot is a cottage, a small house
M is a thousand in Roman numerals, a large number
men are people

explanation.surface: Squeezing a crowd into a tiny home draws complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodating' puts M and MEN inside COT.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark, especially a critical one, is a comment.

clue.text: A man, if preceding the Queen, must be neat

parts.note: he stands for any man
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Etiquette insists a gentleman walking ahead of the monarch be tidily turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, not tidy; a young cow fits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic collective term for cattle, and a young cow that has not calved is one such beast.

clue.text: Dunce near collapse exhibiting fortitude

indicators.note: collapse means falling apart, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A dim pupil close to breaking down shows courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina, the power to hold out through hardship, is fortitude.

clue.text: A growing girl?

parts.note: a girl's name which is also the word for plant life, so this girl literally grows

explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name that is also the collective word for plants, which grow.

clue.text: Not so prudent — really a bit of a pig

explanation.definitionFit: Rasher is comparative of rash, more reckless; a rasher is also a slice of bacon from a pig.

clue.text: Shut down before the end of August for the recess

parts.note: to close is to shut down

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here the last of August

explanation.surface: Shut up shop before the end of August for the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like a holiday but is a small room or cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard or alcove set into a wall is a recess.

clue.text: Adopted a certain attitude as asked

explanation.definitionFit: To strike a pose is to adopt a posture for show; to put a question is likewise said of a query raised.

clue.text: Sweet model distracted by financial obligations

indicators.note: distracted means thrown into confusion, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A fashion model is too worried about debts to concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distracted' turns MODEL into MELOD, followed by IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet of music means tuneful and pleasant to the ear.

clue.text: Her aim is to see everyone well-suited

definitions.text: Her aim is to see everyone well-suited

parts.words: Her aim is to see everyone well-suited
parts.note: well-suited sounds like being happily matched, but here it means dressed in a good suit, which a woman who makes clothes provides

explanation.definitionFit: A woman who cuts and sews made-to-measure garments wants each client fitted out in a good suit.

clue.text: A writer about modern times, note

parts.note: re means concerning or about
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An author who writes about the present day takes a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a nineteenth-century English novelist and dramatist.

clue.text: Taken in hand by the main supervisor

definitions.text: Taken in hand by the main supervisor

parts.words: Taken in hand by the main supervisor
parts.note: the main is the sea, and its supervisor is Neptune, who holds a three-pronged spear

explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, ruler of the sea, is always pictured carrying a three-pronged spear.

clue.text: Occasions when children are not allowed to be choosy

definitions.text: Occasions when children are not allowed to be choosy

parts.words: Occasions when children are not allowed to be choosy
parts.note: choosy hints at choosing, and children cannot vote at the polls when people make choices

explanation.definitionFit: Polls are when adults vote, choosing candidates; minors have no vote.

clue.text: Bid, being vulnerable

explanation.definitionFit: A bid is an offer, as in a formal offer to supply; vulnerable means sore or sensitive to touch.

clue.text: A financial expert comes into organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A money specialist joins a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in the study of money, trade and markets.

clue.text: A good tennis-player (minor) won't give anybody the pip

definitions.text: A good tennis-player (minor) won't give anybody the pip

parts.words: A good tennis-player (minor) won't give anybody the pip
parts.note: a good tennis player is seeded; giving no pips describes fruit with no stones

explanation.walkthrough: To give someone the pip is British slang for annoying them; here it is literal, fruit having no pips.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapes or oranges with no pips are grown without seeds.

clue.text: A six-footer, though not out of school

parts.note: in cricket a batsman still batting is in, not out
a school of thought is a sect

explanation.surface: A very tall person has not yet left school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is a creature with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Every true bug, beetle or fly has six legs, so it is a creature with six feet.

clue.text: Sit up if left within this Georgian city

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so these letters go inside
in a down clue up means the word is read backwards from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Sit up if you are left in this city in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SIT into TIS, and 'within' puts IF and L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for Tbilisi, capital of Georgia in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Awfully mean individual making a bloomer

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A very stingy person makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' turns MEAN into ANEM. 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant is something that blooms, and this one is a spring flower of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Some women fail — men too — giving rise to complaint

indicators.note: some means only part of these words is taken, the letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: Some women fall ill, and men too.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor illness is a complaint.

clue.text: A supporter or two accompanying 23

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
23 across is RIGHT, and R is its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A supporter or two accompanying another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that braces or props up is a support.

clue.text: True blue!

explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of the British Conservative Party, the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: True means correct; blue stands for Conservative, the party of the political wing opposite the left.

clue.text: Newly-wed — a stable fellow

explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom is a man just married; a stable lad caring for horses is also so called.

clue.text: Being a fool, she'd concocted a misleading statement

indicators.note: concocted means made up or mixed together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: She was foolish enough to make up a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is an untrue claim intended to deceive.

clue.text: Added to former expertise when climbing

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: art means skill or expertise

explanation.surface: Something added to past skill when climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, over and above.

clue.text: "How doth the little improving his shining tail." (Lewis Carroll)

definitions.text: "How doth the little improving his shining tail." (Lewis Carroll)

parts.words: "How doth the little improving his shining tail." (Lewis Carroll)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the reptile in Carroll's parody poem in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.walkthrough: The line from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland runs 'How doth the little ... improve his shining tail'; the gap takes a Nile reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's poem parodies Isaac Watts's busy bee with a Nile reptile that welcomes little fishes into its jaws.

clue.text: Stumble bearing rubbish

parts.note: to trip is to stumble
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone trips while carrying a load of junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is offal, and figuratively means nonsense or worthless stuff.

clue.text: Careless soldiers don't .hit the target

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
to miss is to fail to hit a target

explanation.surface: Sloppy troops fail to score on the range.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent in one's duties.

clue.text: The male figures where support is needed

definitions.text: The male figures where support is needed

parts.words: The male figures where support is needed
parts.note: figures here are carved statues of men used in place of columns to hold up a building

explanation.definitionFit: These are sculpted men used as columns, named after the Titan who held up the sky.
